_purpose: Project-scope Claude Code settings. Committed and template-owned: this file syncs to every derived repo, so it may only contain rules that are correct in EVERY repo the template produces, including the template itself.

permissions._deny_note: Deny rules are the most durable control Claude Code offers: per the permission-modes docs they 'block in every mode, including bypassPermissions', and no settings scope can remove a deny another scope added. That absoluteness is also the constraint — a deny here cannot be relaxed downstream, so this list holds ONLY credential and key material that no repo ever has cause to read or hand-edit. Protection of the harness's own governing files (.claude/, .devcontainer/, route-model.sh) is deliberately NOT here: /firewall-allow legitimately edits .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh, and the template repo edits all of them as its product. That protection lives in the PreToolUse hook instead, where it can be conditional. See docs/THREAT_MODEL.md.
permissions._no_bash_denies_note: No Bash deny rules here on purpose. The permissions docs warn that patterns constraining command arguments are fragile — Bash(curl http://github.com/ *) misses -X before the URL, https, -L redirects, variable indirection and extra spaces. A deny list that looks protective but is trivially bypassed is exactly the false assurance this template is trying to stop shipping. Network egress is enforced at the firewall (.devcontainer/init-firewall.sh), which cannot be argued around.

sandbox._note: Requires bubblewrap, added to .devcontainer/Dockerfile alongside this block. Before that, every key here was inert. Enabling the sandbox is also what activates Claude Code's protected paths, which deny a running command writes to .claude/settings*, .claude/hooks, .mcp.json and .git/config so it cannot grant itself permissions mid-run.
sandbox._failIfUnavailable_note: Deliberately NOT set. It would stop Claude Code starting whenever the sandbox cannot initialise — and bubblewrap needs unprivileged user namespaces, which are often unavailable inside Docker. In a file that syncs to every derived repo, that setting would brick Claude Code across the fleet on a host-kernel detail. The cost of leaving it unset is silent degradation to unsandboxed execution, which is precisely the failure mode this template is trying to stop shipping, so scripts/validate-template.sh asserts actual sandbox availability instead of assuming it. Set it to true in managed settings if you control the fleet's kernels.

credentials._note: The sandbox's default read policy is the entire filesystem, and there is no built-in credential deny list — only what is named here is restricted. These are the paths devcontainer.json mounts into the container as named volumes, so they sit directly beside the agent.

sandbox._network_note: No network.allowedDomains list here on purpose. Egress in this devcontainer is already enforced by .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh at the iptables/ipset layer, which is strictly stronger than a per-process allowlist and applies to every binary, not just sandboxed Bash. Duplicating the domain list here would create a second list to keep in sync and a silent drift source between the two. Note the firewall's own limit, documented in docs/THREAT_MODEL.md: it admits the whole GitHub CIDR range, so it bounds WHERE data can go, not WHETHER it leaves.

_pii_shield_note: PII-Shield (gregmos/PII-Shield) anonymizes content before it reaches Claude. It requires a manual per-machine install (Settings > Extensions > drag in the .mcpb file), so it is NOT a control this template ships — treat it as opt-in. See docs/TEMPLATE_GUIDE.md#pii--privacy-controls.
_statusline_note: The caveman statusline badge is auto-configured by scripts/install-caveman.sh at container start into user-level settings (~/.claude/settings.json), because the plugin script lives at a hash-versioned cache path. Do not hardcode a statusLine here.
